summary.text: A 47-year-old non-smoking man weighing 62.1 kg and 166.8 cm tall had a history of operable tongue cancer, treated in his thirties with mandibular resection and plate reconstruction; the infected plate was removed 8 months before presentation. Preoperative spirometry, electrocardiography and transthoracic echocardiogram were normal. He returned for reoperation with a free abdominal muscle flap with vascular anastomosis, partial mandibular resection and tracheostomy.

After surgery he received deep sedation and ventilator management in the ICU for 48 h, initially with iASV changing only the percentage minute volume; his PaO2/FiO2 ratio on entering the ICU was 462. On postoperative day 3 oxygenation worsened and purulent sputum increased. Sputum culture grew Klebsiella pneumoniae and Pseudomonas otitidis, VAP was diagnosed with the ratio down to 171.5, and ampicillin/sulbactam was changed to meropenem.

iASV was continued with PEEP and FiO2 added as automatic settings, delta P kept below 10 cm H2O, and arterial blood gases every 6 h. As oxygenation improved, FiO2 declined to 0.3 and PEEP was then reduced to 5 cm H2O. Two days after the antibiotic change, WBC, CRP and sputum had decreased, indicating resolution of VAP, and mechanical ventilation was withdrawn.

Propofol was stopped after ventilator usage ended, while dexmedetomidine was continued after extubation at night for sleeping. Two days after stopping the ventilator, his respiratory condition was stable and he was transferred to the general ward.
